items: Starting September 28, commuters in the Philippines will face higher fares for public utility vehicles (PUVs) as the Department of Transportation lifted the suspension on previously approved fare increases.

The minimum fare for jeepneys has increased from P13 to P14, while modern jeepneys now charge a minimum of P17, and bus fares have also been adjusted with ordinary buses starting at P15 for the first 5 kilometers.
Ride-hailing services have seen a base fare increase of P20 across all vehicle types, with significant percentage increases for various car types, and taxi flag-down rates have also risen.

MANILA, Philippines – Commuters will pay higher fares for public utility vehicles (PUVs) starting Monday, September 28, after the Department of Transportation (DOTr) lifted the suspension on fare increases approved by the Land Transportation Franchising and Regulatory Board (LTFRB).
The fare increases were originally set to take effect in March but were suspended by President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. amid the conflict in the Middle East, which drove up global oil prices.
The minimum fare for jeepneys increased from P13 to P14. The rate for each succeeding kilometer rose to P2 from P1.80.

blocks.caption: FARE GUIDE. The table shows the fare for public utility jeepneys, effective September 28, 2026.

blocks.text: For modern jeepneys, the minimum fare is now P17 from P15. The rate per succeeding kilometer also went up to P2.40 from P2.20.
The new bus fare structure for Metro Manila is listed as follows:

items: Ordinary buses: P15 for the first 5 kilometers, plus P2.49 for every succeeding kilometer
Airconditioned buses: P18 for the first 5 kilometers, plus P2.98 for every succeeding kilometer.

The rate per kilometer remains at P15, with no additional charge for fractional distances.
P2P bus fares increased by 15% from the existing rates, depending on the route.
For UV Express, the provisional increase is listed as follows:

items: Traditional UV Express: P2.60 per kilometer for traditional UV Express
Modern UV Express: P3 per kilometer

The flag-down rate for airport taxis, meanwhile, increased by P40, or 53%, from P75 to P115 for the first 500 meters.
There will be no changes to the rates for every succeeding 300 meters or each two-minute waiting period.
The fare increases come after different bus operators in the country appealed to the Marcos administration. – Rappler.com
